messages:
elaine (eng-runtime): Heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-selector landing we see a regression in tail latency for hosted streaming. p95 mostly OK, p99 up ~2.2x. digging in now.

sam (eng-ml): ugh. any idea which path? new kernel choice or batching change?

elaine (eng-runtime): initial profiling points at an interaction between the new attention kernel and our microbatch sizing heuristic + KV cache behavior. perf-bot uploaded flamegraphs: https://internal.perf/1712151234/flame.svg

mike (eng-infra): @elaine can you paste the microbatch and flush settings used in the run that regressed?

elaine (eng-runtime): defaults at the time:
```
microbatch_size: auto (target latency 60ms)
stream_chunk_tokens: 64
stream_flush_interval_ms: 200
kv_cache_mode: shared
kernel_selector: use_latest_attention_v2
```

katie (eng-sre): kv cache shared? we recently changed eviction in shared mode, maybe miss rate spiked and caused more recompute. Do we have hit/miss numbers?

perf-bot: Profiling snapshot:
- KV cache hit-rate: 62% (baseline 87%)
- avg tokens/server: +18%
- p95 latency: +15%
- p99 latency: +120%
- observed microbatch distribution: many single-request microbatches at tail
(see /perf/snapshots/1712151234)

sam (eng-ml): If KV hit-rate dropped, more KV fetches cause stalls in the attention kernel, and with larger stream_chunk_tokens the backend holds the tokenization/assembly longer before flush. That could amplify tail latency.

devon (eng-platform): Also note kernel v2 changes kernel launch granularity — slightly higher startup overhead but better throughput at steady-state. That plays badly with small microbatches.

elaine (eng-runtime): Agreed. Hypothesis: kernel_selector picked v2 which increases per-microbatch overhead; microbatch auto falls to smaller sizes for tail, combined with lower KV hit rate -> p99 spikes. Need experiments: 1) force old kernel, 2) larger microbatch floor, 3) decrease stream_flush_interval, 4) KV eviction rollback.

mike (eng-infra): I can spin an A/B: group A pinned to attention_v1, group B stays on v2. Also can run a config with microbatch_floor=8 and flush=50ms. Which metric should we watch? p99_stream_latency and perceived_stream_latency_ms (time to first token rendered).

katie (eng-sre): Add an SLO check: fail if p99 > 250ms for streaming-first-token over 10m window. Also track p95 for throughput regressions.

sam (eng-ml): Small note re flush interval: lowering flush interval reduces perceived latency but increases number of tiny packets (more kernel invocations). For v2 that might hurt. For v1 it might help. So we should test cross-product: (kernel v1/v2) x (flush 50/200) x (microbatch floor 1/8). Keep stream_chunk_tokens at 32 and 64 variants.

elaine (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a job matrix. quick sample results I ran locally:
- v1, flush=50, floor=8, chunk=32 => p99 down 35%, perceived-first-token -120ms
- v2, flush=50, floor=8, chunk=32 => p99 down 5%, increased cpu jumps
- v2, flush=200, floor=1, chunk=64 => p99 +110% (regression)

devon (eng-platform): Good to capture KV metrics per bucket too. If we pin microbatch floor higher we get fewer tiny microbatches and higher chance for prefix KV re-use. That should raise hit-rate back toward baseline.

mike (eng-infra): Ran the A/B for 30m with traffic ramp:
- A (v1 + floor=8 + flush=50): p95=75ms p99=180ms KV-hit=84%
- B (v2 + auto floor + flush=200): p95=90ms p99=440ms KV-hit=63%
Throughput steady. B had more kernel launches per second.

katie (eng-sre): Action: revert kernel_selector to prefer v1 for streaming endpoints until we can tune v2 for microbatch tails. Also set microbatch_floor=4 globally and flush_interval_ms=75 for hosted streaming as a temporary mitigation.

elaine (eng-runtime): I'll open a rollout rollback PR and a config change. Also creating an experiment ticket to optimize v2 for small microbatches (work on kernel launch amortization and KV async warmups).

sam (eng-ml): Long-term: we should adapt kernel selection based on observed microbatch size distribution and KV-hit heuristics at runtime. If most microbatches < threshold, pick low-startup kernel; else pick high-throughput kernel.

devon (eng-platform): +1. Consider a lightweight classifier: if recent tail percentiles of microbatch_size < 4 AND KV-hit < 70% then override to v1. Could be a simple moving-window rule.

mike (eng-infra): Filed infra ticket 8543 for metric dashboards to show microbatch-size histogram + kernel type + KV-hit rate ~ time. Getting that will make future incidents much quicker.

elaine (eng-runtime): Thanks. I'll post PR links when ready. For now rolling back selector to v1 for streaming hosts and applying flush=75 / microbatch_floor=4 as katie suggested.

katie (eng-sre): Noted. I'll keep pager link open and watch p99 for the next 2 hours. :eyes:

perf-bot: Rollback applied to 40% of streaming fleet at 1712153600. Monitoring: preliminary p99 trend returning toward baseline.

elaine (eng-runtime): Great. Postmortem draft after we stabilize: include root cause (v2 start-up cost + KV miss surge + small microbatches), quant numbers, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (autore-selector heuristic, kernel optimizations, KV eviction tuning).

sam (eng-ml): One more thought: token chunk size interacts with perceived latency — smaller chunk tokens (16 vs 64) yields faster first-byte but increases per-token overhead. We should expose chunk size per-customer or auto-tune by SLA tier.

elaine (eng-runtime): Agreed. We'll add chunk auto-tuning to the experiment list. Closing loop once dashboards and kernel fixes land. Thanks everyone.
